pr_body:
Fixes #653 

This allows a user to specify the target directory to clone to as part of the additional arguments.

It's not the prettiest implementation, but it works. It essentially parses the extra args to find any orphaned ones, Ideally we could somehow leverage git's actual command line arg parsing, maybe through something like this. But this is pretty much my first go code, so I wasn't really sure how to go about doing that.

Based on conversation in #721, this functionality was separated into it's own feature.
pr_comments:
Ah, yea. The future compatibility is why I was thinking about using their parser, but your suggestion is :100: better. 

I left `parseExtraArgs` as a separate function for testability and in case there's ever another need to parse the args.
@mislav Thanks for the feedback; I made the requested changes if you want to resolve the conversations.

issue_context.title: repo clone should support cloning into a specific directory
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

`git clone ssh://git@github.com/user/repo.git user_repo` allows you to specify a directory to clone into (`user_repo` here). `gh repo clone` supports passing extra arguments to `git clone` but when using this, it assumes my extra arg is the repo to clone not the path to clone into.

```
[14:59:59] % gh repo clone NARKOZ/gitlab -- narkoz_gitlab
fatal: repository 'narkoz_gitlab' does not exist
exit status 128
```

I saw mention in https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/545 about maybe adding support for this, so I figured I'd ask here for this feature. 

### Proposed solution

I'm not sure how many people (frequently) clone into directories that aren't just named after the project but something like `gh repo clone agargiulo/stuff my_stuff` would be helpful for when I find 3 different projects named the same and want to keep track more easily locally.

### Additional context
comments:
It looks like the issue is in https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/0680bb5c6c230ea6adccbc63c1374fe56d11d971/command/repo.go#L119-L120

Since the extra args are prepended to the repo name, the actual command being run is
```
git clone narkoz_gitlab NARKOZ/gitlab 
```

`git clone` expects an optional directory to come after the repo name [(man page)](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone).

I think the only way this could be accomplished is to essentially run an argparse on `args[1:]` to figure out if there are any bare args are the end. Then if there are, remove them from `args[1:]` and then append then after `cloneURL`.

I'm a go noob, but I'm trying to write up a patch for this. I wrote a failing test you can stick in `repo_test.go` if anybody else is going to work on it.
```
{
  name: "clone arguments with directory",
  args: "repo clone OWNER/REPO -- -o upstream --depth 1 target_directory",
  want: "git clone -o upstream --depth 1 https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.git target_directory",
},
```
